The migration file defines the function signature in the `REVOKE` and `GRANT` statements as `public.insert_mark_decisions(UUID, JSONB)` without any space after the comma. Since `normalizeSql` removes all extra whitespace but does not add spaces, `afterFinalDefinition` will contain `(uuid,jsonb)` instead of `(uuid, jsonb)`. This mismatch will cause the contract test to fail. Removing the space after the comma in the expected string will align the test with the normalized SQL output and maintain stable output contract semantics.

```javascript
    expect(afterFinalDefinition).toContain(
      'revoke execute on function public.insert_mark_decisions(uuid,jsonb) from public, anon, authenticated',
    );
    expect(afterFinalDefinition).toContain(
      'grant execute on function public.insert_mark_decisions(uuid,jsonb) to service_role',
    );
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When parameterizing SQL generation or database queries with dynamic values, ensure that downstream runners or post-processors maintain stable output contract semantics by correctly handling or overwriting the metadata.
</details>

The checked-in migration source is `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.insert_mark_decisions(UUID, JSONB)` and `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.insert_mark_decisions(UUID, JSONB)`, with a space after the comma. `normalizeSql()` collapses that existing whitespace to the single space expected by `(uuid, jsonb)`; it does not remove it. The focused effective migration-order contract now passes 8/8 on head `de50ef1e9`, including the unchanged whitespace expectation, so no expectation change is needed.
